identity.title: High Dense Gas Fraction in Intensely Star-forming Dusty Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA and VLA detections of the dense molecular gas tracers HCN, HCO$^+$ and HNC in two lensed, high-redshift starbursts selected from the *Herschel*-ATLAS survey

question.value: Do lensed high-z dusty starbursts (SDP.9, SDP.11) have dense gas excitation, line ratios and L_IR-L_dense relations like local (U)LIRGs, and is their dense gas fraction higher?

evidence.quote: Our results suggest that the intense star formation found in some high-redshift dusty, luminous starbursts is associated with more massive dense molecular gas reservoirs and higher dense molecular gas fractions.

claims.hypothesis: High-z lensed starbursts follow the local L_IR-L_dense relation
claims.experiment: Compare demagnified L_IR and dense line luminosities with literature
claims.result: Points fall on a single relation with local galaxies; local scatter ±0.5 dex
claims.finding: No evidence of enhanced SFR per dense gas luminosity; higher SFR from more dense gas

evidence.quote: the correlation between IR and line luminosity for both low-redshift galaxies and SDP.9 and SDP.11 can be described by a single relation.

claims.hypothesis: SDP.9 has a higher dense gas fraction
claims.experiment: HCN/CO ratio and M_dense vs M_H2
claims.result: J=1-0 HCN/CO higher than most local sources; M_dense 8.4e10 vs M_H2 1.3e11
claims.finding: Large fraction of gas is dense

evidence.quote: This suggests that a very large fraction of the molecular gas in SDP.9 is in the form of dense gas.

claims.hypothesis: Excitation of SDP.9 is like local IR-bright galaxies

evidence.quote: indicating that the molecular gas in local and high-redshift dusty starbursts can have similar excitation conditions.
